'''Alberto Sergio Cattaneo''' (26 June 1967 in [[Milan]])<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Prof. Alberto S. Cattaneo|website=Institut für Mathematik, Universität Zürich|url=http://user.math.uzh.ch/cattaneo/}}</ref> is an Italian [[mathematician]] and [[mathematical physicist]], specializing in [[geometry]] related to [[quantum field theory]] and [[string theory]].

==Biography==
After attending ''[[Liceo scientifico]]'' ''A. Volta'' in Milan, Cattaneo studied physics at [[University of Milan]], graduating in 1991. In 1995, he obtained a PhD in theoretical physics at the same university; his thesis, entitled ''Teorie topologiche di tipo BF ed invarianti dei nodi'' (Topological [[BF theory|BF theories]] and [[knot invariant]]s), was supervised by Maurizio Martellini.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Alberto Cattaneo - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=120224 |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

Cattaneo worked as a postdoc in 1995-1997 at [[Harvard University]] (with [[Arthur Jaffe]]) and in 1997-1998 at the University of Milan (with [[Paolo Cotta-Ramusino]]). In 1998, he moved to [[University of Zurich]]'s mathematics department as an assistant professor, and he became a full professor in 2003.<ref name="homepage" />

In 2006 he was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers#2006, Madrid|invited speaker]], with the talk ''From topological field theory to deformation quantization and reduction'', at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM2006.2/ICM2006.2.ocr.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician 2006 |publisher=[[European Mathematical Society]] |year=2007 |editor-last=Sanz-Solé |editor-first=Marta |editor-link=Marta Sanz-Solé |location=Madrid |pages=339 |editor-last2=Soria |editor-first2=Javier |editor-last3=Varona |editor-first3=Juan Luis |editor-last4=Verdera |editor-first4=Joan}}</ref> Cattaneo was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Cattaneo's research interests include [[deformation quantization]], [[Symplectic geometry|symplectic]] and [[Poisson geometry]], [[topological quantum field theories]], and the mathematical aspects of perturbative quantization of [[gauge theories]].<ref name="homepage" />

With [[Giovanni Felder]] he developed a [[path integral formulation|path integral]] interpretation of the [[Kontsevich quantization formula|deformation quantization of Poisson manifolds]] (introduced in 2003 by [[Maxim Kontsevich]]),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cattaneo |first1=Alberto |last2=Felder |first2=Giovanni |author-link2=Giovanni Felder |year=2000 |title=A Path Integral Approach to the Kontsevich Quantization Formula |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=212 |issue=3 |pages=591–611 |arxiv=math/9902090 |bibcode=2000CMaPh.212..591C |doi=10.1007/s002200000229 |s2cid=8510811}}</ref> as well as a description of the [[symplectic groupoid]] integrating a [[Poisson manifold]] as an infinite-dimensional [[symplectic quotient]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Cattaneo |first1=Alberto S. |last2=Felder |first2=Giovanni |chapter=Poisson sigma models and symplectic groupoids |author-link2=Giovanni Felder |date=2001 |title=Quantization of Singular Symplectic Quotients |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-0348-8364-1_4 |language=en |location=Basel |publisher=Birkhäuser |pages=61–93 |doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8364-1_4 |isbn=978-3-0348-8364-1|s2cid=10248666 |arxiv=math/0003023 }}</ref>

He supervised 14 PhD students as of 2022.<ref name=":0" />
